advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a plan_review_status test that asserts no runner/LLM invocation (e.g. _CountingFake with calls unchanged, or monkeypatch produce_plan_review_verdict to raise) for both the certified and absent cases.
evidence: Docstring contract: 'NO LLM and NO network: the same fast local reads ... never a billable review.' (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:775-778)
New status tests assert only verdict/ok/sha: 'assert st["ok"] is True and st["verdict"] == "certified"' (test_plan_review_gate.py:1336) — none count runner calls or poison the review pipeline.

The file already has the exact no-LLM assertion idiom: '_CountingFake()' with 'assert runner.calls == first' (test_plan_review_gate.py:1012-1019) and 'monkeypatch.setattr(gate_dispatch, "produce_plan_review_verdict", _boom)' (test_plan_review_gate.py:1099-1106), so the missing coverage is a concrete, cheaply-closable gap.
ABSENCE: no search hit for 'runner', 'network', or a CountingFake in the appended status tests (lines 1329-1377).
advisory.finding: The core contract of plan_review_status / `review-plan --status` — that it makes NO LLM call and NO network call (the cheap, non-billable, audit-non-mutating read that is the entire stated motivation) — is asserted by no test. The new tests check only verdict/ok/verified_at_sha/exit-code. A regression that let the status query fall through to a real review (billable, mutates the audit trail) would pass every new test.
scenarios: A refactor routes plan_review_status through review_plan when no attestation exists, silently making the 'cheap read' billable and audit-mutating — no test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: In a new test, run a review with a _CountingFake, record calls, then call rebar.llm.plan_review_status(...) and assert runner.calls is unchanged; additionally monkeypatch gate_dispatch.produce_plan_review_verdict to raise AssertionError and assert plan_review_status still returns a verdict.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a plan_review_status test for a scoped/attested review that asserts verified_at_sha equals the pinned verified-at-sha (distinct from HEAD), exercising the verified_at_sha_from_manifest branch.
evidence: Docstring: 'the pinned verified-at-sha for a scoped/attested review, else the signed HEAD for an unscoped/local one' (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:784-786)

All new/existing status/gate tests use unscoped review helpers ('_review' → rebar.llm.review_plan default source, test_plan_review_gate.py:130-131); the stale test comment confirms 'nothing scoped → whole-HEAD freshness fails' (test_plan_review_gate.py:235).
ABSENCE: no test constructs a scoped/attested (--source attested) review to hit the verified_at_sha_from_manifest branch.
advisory.finding: The verified_at_sha resolution has two branches — pinned verified-at-sha (scoped/attested review) OR signed HEAD (unscoped/local review) — but every test exercises only the unscoped whole-HEAD path (_review with the default runner). The pinned-pin branch (verified_at_sha_from_manifest), which is the 'moving-base-ref' scoped/attested case the feature is explicitly built for, is never tested, so a regression in pin extraction that silently falls back to HEAD is undetectable.
scenarios: A change breaks verified_at_sha_from_manifest so a scoped review reports the signed HEAD instead of the pinned reviewed sha — the surfaced base ref is wrong precisely for the moving-base scenario, and no test catches it.
